The 59th plenary meeting of the tenth emergency special session of the General Assembly is called to order. The Assembly will continue its consideration of agenda item 5 entitled Illegal Israeli actions on occupied East Jerusalem and the rest of the occupied Palestinian territory. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom.

Thank you, President. It has now been over 400 days since Hamas's abhorrent attacks on Israel on the 7th of October, 2023. Over 400 days that the hostages have been cruelly held in captivity. At the outset, I want to make clear the UK's unequivocal call for the immediate release of the hostages, including British citizen Emily Demari. We call on Hamas to stop their abhorrent crimes and to comply with international law. President, we must see this conflict come to an end. The scale of suffering in Gaza is unimaginable. Famine is imminent in some areas, and the UN has reported a shocking increase in cases of acute malnutrition in children. Lack of access to medical treatment will only compound this devastating issue. The past two months have been the worst for aid access since October 2023. International obligations are abundantly clear. The World Food Programme report found that for more than 50 days, barely any food has entered besieged areas. Israel must ensure sufficient aid reaches civilians in Gaza. I reiterate, there is no excuse for Israel's restrictions on humanitarian assistance. Urgent solutions are required now to prevent the very worst from unfolding. We also remain deeply concerned about civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure caused by IDF activity. In North Gaza, Kamal Adwan Hospital has recently come under fire and seriously injured and sick children remain trapped. Israel must do much more to ensure civilians, medical personnel and humanitarian workers are protected and to ensure compliance with international humanitarian law. President, the United Kingdom voted for the draft resolution put to the Security Council on the 19th of November, which called for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, as well as the immediate and unconditional release of hostages. We regret that the council was unable to reach consensus. The UK remains resolute in our commitment to the vision of the draft resolution and will keep working alongside our partners to bring this war to a close, secure the release of the hostages, deliver a huge scale-up in aid, better protect civilians, and ensure that the UN can deliver in Gaza. That is why we intend to vote in favour of today's General Assembly resolution calling for these steps. The UK will carefully consider our position on any future accountability options produced in a report from the Secretary General. The UK considers, however, that focus should remain on encouraging all parties to cooperate with existing mechanisms of accountability. With this in mind, The UK reiterates its unwavering support to the ICJ while recognizing their recent advisory opinion is, of course, not binding as a matter of international law and that this resolution does not change that. In any event, there remains an imperative need for negotiations between all parties based on a two-state solution recognising the relevant Security Council resolutions. The UK intends to vote in favour of the resolution in support of UNRWA. We unequivocally reject attempts to undermine or degrade UNRWA. As my Foreign Secretary has said, the legislation passed by the Israeli Knesset seeking to restrict UNRWA's work is unacceptable. UNRWA has an unequivocal mandate from the UN membership to provide lifesaving aid to thousands of Palestinians in need. The UK continues to support UNRWA to deliver important reforms which can further strengthen their commitment to neutrality. As the occupying power, Israel has a responsibility to ensure Palestinians have basic services. UNRWA, and UNRWA alone, is equipped to deliver that. Today, my Prime Minister committed to an additional US$16.5 million to UNRWA to support vital services for Palestinian refugees in the OPTs and the wider region. While the UK intends to vote in favour of this resolution, we wish to clarify that our position does not prejudge any future international legal determinations referenced in the text. President, a ceasefire, the release of hostages now held for over 400 days, and urgent steps to address the humanitarian crisis are more critical than ever. We are working urgently with our partners to deliver on this and to give the people of Gaza and of Israel the prospect of a peaceful future that they deserve. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Norway.

Thank you, President.

The conflict between Israel and Hamas has led to enormous civilian suffering.

Norway strongly regrets that the UN Security.

Council in November again failed to unite on a resolution calling for ceasefire in Gaza.

We need an unconditional and permanent ceasefire now. All remaining hostages must be released immediately.

Unrestricted provision of necessary humanitarian aid must be provided to the people of Gaza without delay.

Israel's massive warfare has left Gaza in ruins.

We see a staggering number of civilians being killed and injured, including women and children, every day.

This is completely unacceptable and must stop.

Israeli authorities continue to impede access to food and necessary emergency aid, despite their obligation to secure unimpeded access.

Both into and internally in Gaza. The risk of famine has been imminent for a long time, especially in northern part of Gaza. Norway emphasizes in this regard that starvation of civilians as a method of warfare may constitute a war crime.

President, for more than one year, the Israeli government has systematically obstructed UNRWA.

The backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza, and other organisations providing aid in carrying out their work.

The Knesset legislation adopted on 28 October aims to prevent UNRWA from working in Palestine, effectively crippling the key actor in the middle of a humanitarian catastrophe. Norway condemns these decisions and urges Israel to repeal them. Through these measures, Israel jeopardizes the lives of countless Palestinians, the stability of the region, and ultimately the security of both Israelis and Palestinians.

On behalf of a cross-regional group of countries, Norway will put forward a draft.

Resolution to the UN General Assembly requesting the International Court of Justice to give an advisory opinion.

On Israel's obligations to facilitate humanitarian.

Assistance and other kinds of aid to the Palestinian population delivered by the UN, international organizations and states.

And in fact, this resolution is being uploaded to e-delegate as I speak, and I invite you to co-sponsor it.

Because no country is exempt from its international legal obligations.

No country is above the law.

If we, the international community, do not stand up against those who deliberately undermine international.

Law, we are heading down a very dangerous path. We continue to remind Israel of their obligations under international law, including the provisional measures imposed by the ICJ.

President, in September here in New York, Saudi Arabia, the EU, and Norway launched a global alliance for the implementation of the two-state solution.

The best way to bring about peace, stability, and security for Israel, for Palestine, and for the region.

Is through the realization of the Palestinian state and the two-state solution.

Lately, members of the Israeli government have openly been calling for applying sovereignty in the West Bank, a clear step.

Towards illegal annexation. Norway condemns any action and rhetoric aimed at impeding the full realization of the Palestinian state and the two-state solution, including any attempt at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip. Let us commit to taking concrete and irreversible steps towards a two state solution. For the record, Norway will support the two resolutions put forward today.
I thank the distinguished representative of Norway. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

Mr. President, today the situation in occupied Palestine territory, including Gaza Strip, is critical and severe beyond imagination. Since the beginning of the Israeli genocidal attack, over 44,000 Palestinians, particularly women and children, have been killed, and unprecedented humanitarian crisis has taken place. due to past destruction of homes, schools, hospitals, spread of disease, forced displacement and mass detention. We express deep condolence to the Palestinian victims of the Israeli genocide and their bereaved families, and condemn in strongest terms the genocidal attack by Israel in occupied Palestinian territory in flagrant violation of the UN Charter and international law. It is imperative for international community to put an end urgently Israel's decade-long illegal occupation of Palestinian territory and redouble its efforts to immediately advance process of accountability for all war crimes committed by Israel against the people of Palestine and the other nationalities. Mr. President, The international community has made tireless efforts for several decades to put an end to Israel's illegal occupation and realize the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people. However, the fair and just solution to the Palestinian issue remains deadlocked, and the situation in occupied Palestinian territory and the rest of the Middle East region is increasingly becoming aggravated. It is entirely attributable to the unilateral and hegemonic policy and double standard of the United States, which has connived at and patronized Israeli illegal territorial expansion. As is widely known, since outbreak of the Gaza crisis, United States has persistently provided Israel with a huge amount of the military, financial, and logistical support, tasking the light to mass atrocities of Israel. Worse still, United States cast the veto six times at the Security Council on the draft resolutions calling for immediate, permanent, and unconditional ceasefire in Gaza Strip. Such United States unilateral and shameful approach is adding fuel to the already aggravated situation which triggered surge indignation and condemnation from international community. The above fact clearly prove that it's none other than the United States that desperately obstruct the peaceful settlement of Palestinian issue equally aspired by international community. As long as the United States continues to resort to biased and double dealing in favor of patronizing and backing Israel's act of territorial extortion and mass killings, peace and stability can never settle down in the Middle East. International community should resolutely denounce and reject the unilateral and double standard moves of the United States to aggravate the situation of the region. It should take a decisive step to frustrate such United States moves through advanced solidarity and concerted actions. In conclusion, we reaffirm our commitment to support for and solidarity with the Palestinian people in their just struggle to terminate Israel's illegal occupation and to realize their inalienable rights, including self-determination and establishment of an independent state with East Jerusalem as its capital. Also, we fully support accession of the State of Palestine as a full-fledged UN member state. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Zimbabwe.

Mr. President, thank you for convening this session, which has been prompted by the recent failure by the United Nations Security Council to adopt a resolution that was a pathway to securing an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire alongside the immediate and unconditional release of hostages. Furthermore, the resolution would have laid the foundation for addressing the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. Mr. President, over the years, we have witnessed a growing number of vetoes on resolutions concerning the question of Palestine. Each successive veto has perpetuated the conflict, prolonged civilian suffering, and diminished the prospects for a just and lasting peace. These vetoes are preventing the Security Council from responding timely to the crisis in Gaza, thereby undermining the Council's credibility and effectiveness. This underscores the urgent need for Security Council reform to ensure that this principal organ of the United Nations can address global challenges impartially. Mr. President, last week, the permanent observer of the State of Palestine delivered a harrowing account of the situation in Gaza. More than 44,000 Palestinians have lost their lives since 7 October 2023, the majority of whom are women and children. More than 300 United Nations and humanitarian staff operating in Gaza have also lost their lives as a result of this unjust conflict. Furthermore, humanitarian efforts are being hampered as aid agencies are failing to deliver critical supplies of food and medicine. At the same time, the operations of UNRWA, which is providing life-saving services to the Palestinians across the Middle East, are being threatened by the recently adopted Israeli legislation. UNRWA must be allowed to carry out its vital work without interruption or politicization. Mr. President, My delegation recalls the various Security Council resolutions that have already been adopted, including resolution 2735, and calls for their full implementation. The full implementation of these binding resolutions will affirm the Palestinians' rights to self-determination, alleviate the humanitarian crisis, end the occupation, promote regional stability, unlock the economic potential in Palestine, and reaffirm our commitment to international law, human rights, and the UN Charter. Mr. President, as I conclude, my delegation reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people and its commitment to their right to self-determination, peace, and dignity. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Zimbabwe. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Sierra Leone.

Mr. President, Sierra Leone aligns itself with the statement delivered by the representative of Malta on behalf of the 10 elected members of the Security Council. We call the Security Council's meeting on 20th November 2024. Under the agenda item, the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestine question, where we considered a draft resolution calling for a ceasefire in the Gaza Strip. We express our gratitude to the E10 coordinator, Guyana, for their commendable efforts in facilitating the negotiations. Sierra Leone voted in favor of the E10 draft resolution. driven by our unwavering commitment to securing a ceasefire and most importantly to saving lives. We deeply regret that the resolution was not adopted despite 14 members of the Council, an overwhelming majority, voting in favour. With the same urgency to save lives, achieve an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, secure the release of the remaining hostages held by Hamas, and increase the scale of humanitarian assistance to Gaza, Sierra Leone welcomes the draft resolutions to be acted upon by this Assembly. The vote will cast in support of the draft resolution will reflect Sierra Leone's consistent position over the past 14 months following the 7th October 2023 attacks by Hamas, and the response by Israel. With over 44,500 deaths, hundreds of thousands injured, and around 1.7 million internally displaced, the toll on women, children, and the youth is staggering. The need for a ceasefire and the release of all hostages has become urgently overdue. international law unequivocally prohibit conduct that result in devastating and inhumane consequences for civilians during armed conflict so jointly call for all parties to the conflict to comply with the obligations under international law and to ensure that the civilian population in Gaza has access to essential services and humanitarian assistance which are critical for their survival We also acknowledge the vital role of UNRWA in facilitating and distributing aid to civilians. We reiterate the necessity for all parties to the conflict to meet their legal, political, moral, and humanitarian obligations towards the civilians in Gaza and the hostages. Through these resolutions that we'll adopt, we'll seek a further path to justice and accountability. As the United Nations, we must seize this opportunity to reaffirm our role and unite in our collective strength to prevent further destruction and suffering. Mr. President, Serlon welcomes the letter of the Secretary-General bringing to the attention of the General Assembly on an urgent basis two legislations which the Knesset of Israel adopted on 28 October 2024, and which, if implemented, could prevent the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East, UNRWA, from continuing its essential work in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, as mandated by the General Assembly. We note with concern, and as highlighted in the Secretary-General's letter, that these legislations, if implemented, could have serious implications for UNRWA's ability to carry out its activities in the occupied Palestinian territory and more broadly in the region, as mandated by this Assembly. In that vein, we reiterated Secretary-General's assessment that UNRWA is the principal means by which essential assistance is delivered to Palestinian refugees in the occupied Palestinian territory, and there is no realistic alternative to UNRWA that could adequately provide the services and assistance required, whether it be other United Nations entity, other international organizations, or any other entity. The cessation of or restrictions on its activities will leave Palestinians without the essential assistance they require. In closing, let me remember all humanitarian workers who have made the ultimate sacrifice and those serving selflessly in Gaza and the region under extreme conditions to provide critical assistance to those in need. We reiterate our full support to UNRWA and recognize the agency's essential role in delivering lifesaving humanitarian support to the Palestinian people. And I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Sierra Leone. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Angola.

Mr. President, Excellencies, distinguished delegates, allow me to congratulate you, Mr. President, for resuming this tense emergency special session. Angola aligns itself with the statement delivered by Uganda on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. I'll make some additional remarks in my national capacity. Mr. President, the resumption of this emergency special session takes place in a very challenging time and complex context, particularly due to the strategic concerns and regional implication in the political and diplomatic environment in the Middle East and the grave deterioration of the humanitarian and security situation in the Gaza Strip. While we meet at this emergency special session, millions of civilians are suffering and dying every day. In this conflict, there are no winners. All are victims. Civilians, majority women and children, are paying a heavy price, losing everything in many occasions, including their own lives. We condemn terrorism in all its forms and manifestation, regardless of its motivation or actors. Moreover, we call on all concerned parties to the Gaza conflict to exercise the utmost restraint, put an end to all hostilities immediately, and fully abide by international law, including international humanitarian law. Mr. President, This conflict needs to come to an end. The immediate implementation of ceasefire can no longer wait. Full and unlimited humanitarian assistance must be granted. All hostages must be released unconditionally. The time for our collective action is now for the sake of those in the Gaza Strip who see these organizations as their very last hope to achieve peace and stability. UNRWA has been providing for education and providing lifesaving assistance to more than 500,000 Palestinian children in the occupied territories, mainly through the nearly 700 schools it operates. In this context, The cessation or restriction of the activity of UNRWA would leave Palestinian refugees without the essential assistance that they require. The Republic of Angola expresses, therefore, its concern about the dire humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. and considers that any move to prevent the presence of UNRWA undermines fundamental human rights, including the right to life, health, food, water, and sanitation, and increases the tension in this very volatile region. Mr. President, the United Nations, namely the Security Council, must take concrete steps to implement its own resolutions. by creating the independent sovereign state of Palestine. Angola reaffirms the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, including their right to have an independent state, and calls on the Security Council to admit Palestine as a UN full member. We believe that the two-state solution is the only viable option to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. It provides the foundation for the existence of the state of Israel and the state of Palestine living close together in peace and harmony, cooperating in normal way as is supposed to happen between neighboring countries that share common borders and opportunity for bilateral cooperation. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Angola. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Bahrain.

Mr. President, at outset, I wish to thank you for resuming the 10th Emergency Special Session of the General Assembly. I align myself with the statements made by the GCC, the Arab Group, the OIC, and NAM. Mr. President, this meeting is convened in the wake of the incapacity of the Security Council to adopt a draft resolution that calls for, inter alia, an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in the Gaza Strip, one year after the onset of the war against the Gaza Strip, while the risk of escalation continues to threaten regional stability. Amid the current unprecedented and disastrous humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip, we renew our call for an immediate ceasefire and for the unhindered and unconditional delivery of urgent humanitarian assistance to the Gaza Strip to alleviate the stark suffering of the population of Gaza. The Kingdom of Bahrain stresses that the international community must shoulder its responsibilities under the present circumstances and the implementation of United Nations resolutions on the cessation of hostilities and the provision of protection to civilians under IHL, in addition to the release of all detainees and hostages, the provision of safe corridors for the delivery of relief and humanitarian assistance, to the population of Gaza, the reconstruction of devastated areas, and the provision of support to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East as it seeks to fulfill the mandate with which it was entrusted by the General Assembly. Mr. President, the Kingdom of Bahrain reiterates its steadfast position, namely, Its call for the prioritization of dialogue and peaceful means for durable and comprehensive and just peace to prevail in the Middle East, including a ceasefire in the Gaza Strip and the resolution of the Palestinian question based on the two-state solution in accordance with the norms of international law and the resolutions of international legitimacy. In this regard, During the 33rd Arab Summit, the Kingdom of Bahrain has provided a number of initiatives serving various central questions to ensure the stability and development of the region, namely the call for an international conference for peace in the Middle East, the full recognition of the state of Palestine and the acceptance of its membership at the United Nations. We also support the global alliance for the implementation of the two-state solution spearheaded by the sister kingdom of Saudi Arabia. We've welcomed the agreement on the ceasefire in the Republic of Lebanon through the mediation by the United States and France as an important step for the escalation and the reduction of regional military tension. We stress once more that all parties must abide by an immediate and comprehensive and permanent ceasefire and must implement Security Council Resolution 1701 with all its provisions and allow for the establishment of state control across all Lebanese territories. In conclusion, Mr. President, we stress that there is a need for the international community to adopt an irreversible and credible pathway for the establishment of the independent and sovereign Palestinian state along the 4th of June, 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. The Kingdom will continue to support all efforts aimed at ensuring comprehensive and durable peace so as to guarantee security and prosperity for all countries of the region. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Bahrain. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of San Marino.

Mr. President, I thank you for convening this emergency special session following the veto cast in the Security Council on 20 November in accordance with General Assembly resolution 76/262. San Marino thanks the elected 10 Security Council members for drafting a resolution which, if adopted, would have unequivocally demanded the cessation of hostilities through an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, as well as the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other armed groups since the attacks of 7 October. We deeply regret that the text was vetoed. The Security Council must fulfil its responsibility and take action in order to put an end to the destruction in Gaza. Without rapid and collective action, civilians will continue to pay the burden of this conflict. San Marino reiterates its call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Mr. President, San Marino also reiterates its condemnation of the horrible terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October 2023, calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and recognizes Israel's right to defend itself in line with international law. We deplore the unacceptable number of civilian casualties, especially women and children, in Gaza and the West Bank. as well as the catastrophic levels of hunger and imminent risk of famine caused by the insufficient entry of aid into Gaza following Israel's response to these attacks. Rapid, safe, and unimpeded humanitarian access is an obligation under international law. It is essential to ensure urgent humanitarian aid to quickly reach the Palestinian population. In this respect, let me underscore the importance of UNRWA, which provides essential humanitarian assistance to millions of people in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. San Marino is deeply concerned with the recent developments that would hinder the crucial mandate of UNRWA, and we condemn any action aiming at obstructing this agency's capacity to fulfill its mandate. Mr. President, we reiterate our call to all parties to comply with their obligation under humanitarian human rights law and international humanitarian law, including the principle of protection of civilians and their infrastructures of medical facilities, schools, and UN premises. There must be accountability for any violation of international law on all sides. In this respect, we reiterate our full support to the ICC, whose work is crucial in the fight against impunity for genocide and crimes against humanity. Moreover, San Marino alights the need to fully implement the International Court of Justice orders. Mr. President, San Marino remains committed to the realization of a lasting and sustainable peace based on a two-state solution under which the states, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security and mutual recognition. international community must work together in order to restore hope and security to Israelis and Palestinians through a renewed peace process. In this respect, we welcome the decision to hold an international conference under UN auspices next June. Mr President, San Marino will vote today in favour of the two resolutions. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of San Marino. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Papua New Guinea.

Mr. President, the spotlight in the General Assembly on the Security Council's mandate continues apace, and rightly so, given the importance of the Council's members to step up to the plate to honor their commitment and obligations to serve the cause of peace and security for all of humanity. Papua New Guinea is well cognizant of the outcome of the Council's meeting last month that necessitated the continuation today of the General Assembly's dialogue. Let me place on record that Papua New Guinea, as a peace-loving country, wishes for peace, security, and stability at all levels, including in the Middle East region, and particularly in Israel and Palestine. The dire humanitarian situation in Palestine is indeed a shared concern for all peace-loving nations and peoples, including my own country, as is the ongoing security concerns, not only for Palestinians, but also for the state of Israel. Papua New Guinea notes that all lives matter, and needs to be respected and requires an environment of peace and security. Any lasting peace and security for the Israeli-Palestinian situation requires genuine and mutually respectful direct dialogue on all relevant issues by all parties concerned, particularly the Israelis and Palestinians. This includes Israel's right to self-defense as permitted under international law. In our view, rhetoric from any parties that incites harmful, emotive tensions must be avoided, as this is unhelpful for finding the much-needed pathway for peace and security to take root. Mr. President, the most recent murder of an American hostage held by Hamas is strongly deplored and condemned. We renew our call on those holding the hostages from Israel and several other countries to release them without any preconditions and without any further delay. The ceasefire call without the release of all the hostages is unhelpful to the situation. In closing, Mr. President, Papua New Guinea wishes to place on record that though we are a member of the Non-Aligned Movement, we disassociate ourselves from the NAM statement delivered by the delegation of Uganda as the chair of the Coordinating Bureau of the Non-Aligned Movement and the associated co-sponsorship of today's proceedings. We do so because elements contained therein are inconsistent with our national position on the issues raised in the statement and co-sponsorship of this meeting. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Papua New Guinea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Lesotho.

Mr. President, Excellencies, distinguished delegates, Lesotho aligns itself with the statement delivered by the Republic of Uganda on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement at the opening of this session. There is no doubt that the ongoing war in Gaza is one of the most disturbing humanitarian crises recorded in the 21st century. This situation has consequently spawned rippling effects across the region. Despite several calls by the international community for an immediate ceasefire, the war continues unabated. The undue suffering that this conflict has inflicted on women, children, and other vulnerable groups is a total breach of international law and a direct contravention of the principles of the Charter of the United Nations. As a result, we call for an immediate end to this conflict. My delegation is gravely concerned with the challenges facing the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees in the Near East, UNRWA. While it is our collective effort to resolve the Palestinian plight, there is no justification to restricting UNRWA to fulfill its mandate. Such acts, sadly, will collapse the agency and exacerbate further the already daunting humanitarian crisis in Gaza and other Palestinian occupied territories. UNRWA is a lifeline for Palestinian refugees. Any attempts to stifle it from performing its duties will concomitantly lead to a deprivation of essential services, food, education, medical supplies to the children of Gaza, in direct contravention of the commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, among other international instruments. We will recall that in December 2023, this august body adopted a resolution calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a total cessation of hostilities by the protagonists. Furthermore, the General Assembly demanded the unhindered provision of essential aid to civilians in Gaza. However, it is worrisome that today as we speak, the situation in Gaza and other occupied Palestinian territories has become even more catastrophic, particularly with the current challenges faced by UNRWA. We deplore this situation by recalling that the Security Council adopted its landmark resolution 2417 in 2018, strongly condemning the use of food insecurity and starvation as a weapon of war. In closing, Mr. President, The Souto Accord is a call by the UN Secretary-General to all parties involved in the Palestinian conflict to choose peace over war. We call on all the belligerents to lay down their arms and engage in genuine dialogue. On the other hand, we applaud countries that have to date spared no effort towards finding a mediated solution to this conflict. We continue to call for sustained engagements towards finding a lasting solution which respects the rights and concerns of both parties. My country continues to advocate for a two-state solution, which will pave the way for the Israelis and Palestinians to coexist peacefully in line with UN resolutions. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Lesotho. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of China.

President, today we're meeting in this hall for the emergency special session of the General Assembly. This is because the U.S. has once again single-handedly exercised its veto, paralyzing the Security Council and preventing it from taking the necessary actions to promote a ceasefire in Gaza. On the question of Palestine, the No vote cast by the U.S. is an abuse of use of veto. There is no justification whatsoever. To ameliorate the detrimental effects of the veto, Indonesia and other countries have submitted two draft resolutions. One demands an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza and the removal of obstacles to humanitarian access, and the other calls on Israel to rescind the legislation against UNRWA so as to guarantee its normal functioning. It also appeals to the international community to scale up its support to the agency. The two draft resolutions speak volumes to the call for justice by the international community. China will vote in favor of the two draft resolutions. The conflict has dragged on for 14 months. Gaza has been reduced to rubble and ruin. More than 40,000 Palestinians have been killed. The survivors, deprived of the most basic necessities, are struggling in despair. This is a disaster of unprecedented scale. We watched the indiscriminate bombing and disregard for civilian life reach appalling proportions. We witnessed a certain country's unscrupulous moves to condone and shield its ally. We have noticed the selective application of the international law and the use of double standards, the likes of which we have never seen before. One cannot help but wonder, Have the rules and systems established by the UN over its 80 years of existence have become completely irrelevant and useless? Is the world going back to the age where the law of the jungle rule the day? Our answer is this, the world cannot go back to the age of the jungle, nor should the law of the jungle become the new normal. We must push for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire in Gaza. A ceasefire is a prerequisite for saving lives and restoring peace. Linking the ceasefire to other issues, Or even conversely, setting preconditions for a ceasefire, in fact, is tantamount to greenlighting the continuation of war and condoning the continuation of killing. We must uphold the authority of international law. There must be no exceptions in fulfilling obligations under international law. Israel, as the occupying power, must assume its obligations under the IHL and effectively remove all impediments to international, to humanitarian access, ensuring the orderly distribution of goods throughout Gaza and guarantee the safety and security of the humanitarian agencies and their personnel. Inter alia, we need to support the, and guarantee the normal functioning of UNRWA. The agency is a source of support for millions of Palestinian refugees in the region. More importantly, for the people of Gaza, it is a lifeline that has no substitute. We urge Israel to cease its suppression and restriction imposed on humanitarian organizations such as UNRWA. We call on traditional donor countries to continue with their support to UNRWA and refrain from participating in the collective punishment of the Palestinian people. We must revitalize the two-state solution with the utmost urgency, that the two states living side by side and sharing security and development is the only way to achieve peace for Palestine and Israel. The international community should bolster support and provide assurance for the realization of the two-state solution. At present, it is necessary to help the Palestinians to strengthen their governance capacity and support them in reaching agreement on the future arrangement for Gaza through internal consultations. At the same time, it is important to be vigilant and reject any unilateral moves that erode the foundation of the two-state solution, including further expansion of settlements in the West Bank, and attempts to annex the West Bank. China supports the state of Palestine in becoming a full member of the UN. We support the holding of a larger scale, more authoritative, and more effective international peace conference to formulate a timetable and roadmap for the implementation of the two-state solution. China will continue to make unremitting efforts towards an early end to the fighting, restoration of peace in the region and realization of comprehensive, just and lasting solution to the question of Palestine. Thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of China. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Finland.

Mr President, Finland is deeply concerned about the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. The destruction is massive and the horrific civilian death toll is further increasing. The entire Palestinian population in northern Gaza is at imminent risk of dying from disease, famine and violence. The disregard for human life must stop. Finland reiterates its strongest condemnation of the brutal attacks committed by Hamas and other terrorist groups in October last year and taking of hostages in October. But we have consistently underlined that when exercising the right to self defence, international and humanitarian law apply fully. Israel must comply with its obligations under international law in all circumstances. An immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire is needed urgently, and all remaining hostages must be immediately and unconditionally released. All parties must fully comply with international law, including international humanitarian law. UNRWA remains the backbone of the humanitarian response in Gaza. All parties must enable the agency to carry out its mandate as adopted by the General Assembly and its vital services to the civilians in all occupied territories. According to international humanitarian law, All parties to a conflict must allow and facilitate the provision of humanitarian assistance to affected populations. Israel, as the occupying power, has the duty to ensure that the basic needs of the occupied population are met. We call on Israel to enable full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access across the Gaza Strip. Finland's support to rules-based multilateralism with the UN at its core is unwavering. Upholding international law is a shared responsibility of all states. In the midst of an ongoing catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, a halt to any of the activities of UNRWA would have devastating consequences for the hundreds of thousands of civilians served by it. We urge Israel to ensure that UNRWA is allowed to carry out its crucial work in line with its mandate adopted by the UN General Assembly. Mr President, all permanent members of the Security Council bear a special responsibility to exercise their veto in accordance with the letter and spirit of the Charter. On 20 November, a permanent member of the Council, the United States, used a veto against the resolution calling for a ceasefire and release of hostages in Gaza. The General Assembly may discuss any questions relating to the maintenance of international peace and security brought before it by any member of the United Nations. As the Security Council failed again in acting on a situation urgently threatening international peace and security, the General Assembly must act. The situation in Gaza is too dire for the UN to remain silent. Palestinian civilians have borne the brunt of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza for over a year. Their suffering must stop. We, as the international community, must bear our responsibility in urging and assisting the parties to end this conflict and set up a credible process towards a negotiated two state solution, which is the only way to bring lasting peace and security to the Middle East. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Finland. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Canada.

Thank you, President. Canada's position on issues related to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is always guided by our commitment to a framework that best guarantees peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians. It is also guided by our collective obligations to respect international law. We deplore the loss of innocent lives in this conflict and we recognize the direct impact that this situation is still having on countries in the region and elsewhere. All peoples, all countries have been profoundly traumatized by this terrible year of pain, of loss and suffering. We must all be aware of the measures that are needed to establish lasting peace. Canada will today vote in favour of these two resolutions because of the urgent and growing need to resolve this crisis. Canada's votes today underscore our appeals for an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and an increase in humanitarian aid to Gaza, and it is also reaffirmation of our support to the United Nations Relief and Works Agencies for Palestinian Refugees in the Near East, UNRWA. We do not agree with some of the elements included in this resolution. We continue to believe that these resolutions should condemn the horrific terror attacks carried out by Hamas, including on the 7th of October, and Hamas' use of human shields. We would also have liked to see more focus placed on the need for parties to the conflict to negotiate in a significant way on an immediate ceasefire. Canada condemns unequivocally the terrorist attacks carried out against Israel by Hamas on the 7th of October 2023 and the acts of terror that continue. We continue to demand that Hamas put down their weapons to stop using recourse to violence and to immediately release all hostages and the remains of deceased hostages, including the remains of Canadian citizen Judith Weinstein. We are satisfied to see included in the resolution on the ceasefire a call for the release of hostages, and their detention can in no way be continued.

Mr President, we see and feel the terrible damage that is taking place in Gaza, the loss of life, the numbers of those injured. We know that the humanitarian situation is horrific, and it continues to worsen. We mourn all civilians killed since October 7th. The scale of civilian casualties is truly heartbreaking. It is also unacceptable, as all actors must comply with international law. Attacks on humanitarian delivery of food and necessary supplies must also stop. And we need to take note of the serious peace and security situation itself within Gaza when it comes to the delivery of humanitarian services. We have concluded that UNRWA's role in responding to this crisis is crucial. Canada reaffirms its commitment to UNRWA, and we have also recommitted our funding, as have condemned the legislation passed by the Israeli Knesset on October the 28th, which we continue to regret. because we believe that it threatens to prevent UNRWA's vital work in Gaza, the West Bank, and East Jerusalem without ensuring a credible and practical alternative. We continue to press Israel not to implement this legislation, to enable the continuation of UNRWA's activities in education, health services, and to work constructively to enable its crucial role in the delivery of humanitarian assistance. UNRWA's efforts to address allegations against its staff and its willingness to pursue and implement reform of internal processes in line with the independent review of April 2024 led by Catherine Colonna on UNRWA neutrality, these efforts must continue. We call on UNRWA to continue its path of reform as a priority, demonstrating its commitment to the principle of neutrality, and ensure that its activities remain entirely in line with its humanitarian mandate. Canada will continue to actively monitor and support this process of reform and implementation of the Kelowna recommendations. We would ask that anyone, and any country, with additional information or evidence, share this in an open and transparent manner so that it can be dealt with in a proper fashion. Let us be clear that Canada remains opposed to the disproportionate singling out of Israel alone for criticism. We reiterate the importance of a fair-minded approach at the United Nations, and we will not support resolutions that do not, that fail to address the complexities of these issues. The Assembly's work in recent months on the issue of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is a reminder to all of us that in line with the Charter, discussion of such complex issues is not, in fact, reserved entirely for the Security Council. There are options to enable a broader discussion, particularly when the Council cannot act. As President of ECOSOC, I convened a discussion on Haiti just last month to bring attention to the deteriorating situation there, and I hope that this Assembly will find a way to address crucial issues where we find that the Council is stuck, and stuck it surely is, including on Myanmar, Ukraine, Sudan, Afghanistan, Syria, and many other areas of conflict. As we head into the new year, this Assembly must assume its own responsibilities. Canada remains committed to the two-state solution. We believe that a political solution is absolutely essential in order to get to the roots of this conflict and, in fact, to resolve it. We believe that at a time when the dynamics in the broader region show that conflict management, as opposed to conflict resolution, is not a sustainable path to returning the region to a peaceful and prosperous trajectory, we must all do more within our powers, within our capabilities and capacities to listen to each other, to understand that there is no hierarchy in suffering, to demonstrate a capacity to show empathy for all those who have suffered and all those who are suffering. to push hard for the principle of accountability under the rule of law, and to do everything we can in our capacity to resolve this terrible conflict. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

I thank the distinguished representative of Canada. We have heard the last speaker in the debate on this item. The General Assembly has thus concluded this stage of its consideration of agenda item five. The Assembly will resume its consideration of agenda item five entitled Illegal Israeli Actions in Occupied East Jerusalem and the Rest of the Occupied Palestinian Territory to take action on two draft resolutions, issued as documents A/ES-10/L.32 and A/ES-10/L.33. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Ireland to introduce draft resolution A/ES-10/L.32.

President, Excellencies, distinguished delegates, it is an honor for Ireland to introduce the draft resolution entitled Support for the Mandate of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East, UNRWA, as contained in document L-32, which has been submitted to the General Assembly for adoption in this resumed 10th Emergency Special Session. At the outset, I want to thank all the 50 plus member states who have co-sponsored this resolution. We, the co-sponsors, present this draft resolution at a time of profound challenge to the continuity of UNRWA's operations and its lifesaving assistance to millions of Palestine refugees, as well as to an important contribution to regional stability. We present this draft in the context of shocking developments in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, and especially in the Gaza Strip over the past 14 months. Our action comes in the wake of appeals for decisive intervention by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and UNRWA Commissioner-General Philippe Lazarrini. Earlier this week, the Secretary-General circulated a letter on enabling UNRWA to carry out its activities. This followed an extraordinary letter in October to the President of the General Assembly, in which Commissioner-General Lazarrini warned that the agency was under such physical, political, and operational attack, unprecedented in the UN's history, that implementation of its mandate may become impossible without decisive action by this General Assembly. President, this draft resolution is the co-sponsor's response. We appeal to all states and members of the General Assembly to act with urgency and resolve to confirm your support for UNRWA's mandate. This is essential to avoid any interruption or suspension of UNRWA's vital humanitarian and development programmes, including education for hundreds of thousands of children. President, over the past 14 months, UNRWA has faced repeated attacks from Israel. It has been subject to attempts by the Israeli government to dismantle the agency and evict it from its premises in occupied East Jerusalem through the adoption of legislation by the Israeli Knesset. It has faced military attacks on its personnel and facilities and has been a target of a dangerous campaign of misinformation and disinformation. Commissioner General Nazzareni warned in stark terms that the risk of the agency's collapse threatens the lives and the futures of individuals and communities, the stability of the region and the integrity of our multilateral system. We recall too that earlier this month, the Interagency Standing Committee, the highest level humanitarian coordination forum, called for a halt to the assault on Palestinians in Gaza and on those trying to help them. The committee warned of the disastrous impact of Israel's legislation against UNRWA, stating that if implemented, such measures would be a catastrophe for the humanitarian response in Gaza, would be diametrically opposed to the UN charter, and would have potentially dire impacts on the human rights of the millions of Palestinians depending on UNRWA's assistance, in violation of Israel's obligations under international law. They further aligned that there is no alternative, no alternative to UNRWA. We echo their urgent warnings today. We underscore UNRWA's essential and irreplaceable role as unequivocally reaffirmed in the shared commitments on UNRWA launched in July of this year. UNRWA's mandate is an integral part of the UN's longstanding responsibility on the question of Palestine. It will remain so until a just solution is found, including for the plight of the Palestine refugees in line with Resolution 1943. It must be given the necessary political and financial support, including sustained and predictable funding, to ensure the continuity of its operations in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, and the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, without interruption or impediment in accordance with the mandate conferred by this Assembly. We call on Israel not to implement the recent legislation against UNRWA and to cease all attempts to interfere, obstruct, undermine, dismantle, or spread misinformation or disinformation about the agency. Israel must respect the agency's privileges and immunities as a UN entity, and it must fulfill its international legal obligations, including under international humanitarian law. President, we pay tribute to UNRWA's staff for their dedicated service even in the most dire conditions and at great personal danger to their own lives. We express our condolences to the families, friends, and colleagues of the 252 UNRWA staff members tragically killed over the past year in the occupied Palestinian territory, the overwhelming majority in Gaza. This is the highest number of casualties suffered by humanitarians and by the UN in any conflict since the organization's establishment, and we stress the imperative of ensuring accountability. We commend UNRWA's Commissioner General for his leadership and his staff for their tireless efforts to deliver on UNRWA's mandate and their commitment to uphold the humanitarian principles of neutrality, independence, impartiality, and humanity, and to fully implement the recommendations of the Kholana report. The General Assembly must act swiftly to safeguard the mandate of UNRWA to ensure the well-being, development, and protection of Palestine refugees in all five fields of operation, and to sustain its long-term investment in peace, pending the achievement of a just solution, including for the plight of the Palestine refugees. We must redouble our efforts to support the agency and to prevent any further obstruction of its indispensable and lifesaving assistance in the face of the catastrophic situation in Gaza. The refugee population has suffered repeated dispossession, displacement, and trauma for decades. UNRWA is indispensable to civilians facing military attack, hunger, disease, poverty, loss of learning and livelihoods, denial of humanitarian access, mass forced displacement and mass destruction of civilian infrastructure. It simply must be protected. We must act swiftly to ensure the protection of the Palestinian civilian population including by ensuring the provision of immediate, unimpeded humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza, with UNRWA playing its indispensable humanitarian role and serving as the backbone of the UN humanitarian delivery system. We must act now in line with our collective obligations under international law, including humanitarian and human rights law, to preserve UNRWA, a lifeline for the well-being, sustenance, hope, and dignity of millions of refugees and displaced civilians. We must also make every effort to make a just and peaceful resolution of the Palestine question in all its aspects a reality, in accordance with international law and relevant UN resolutions. In closing, President, on behalf of the co-sponsors, Ireland calls on all states and members of the General Assembly to vote in favor of the draft resolution contained in document L32. We express our deep appreciation in advance to all delegations upholding their international legal obligations and rising to the historic responsibility we must all bear at this time of grave, grave crisis. I thank you, President.

Mr. President, Indonesia is honored to introduce draft resolution L-33 entitled, "Demand for Ceasefire in Gaza," in this resumed 10th Emergency Special Session of the General Assembly. This resolution presented amid an unprecedented and devastating crisis on the Palestinian people in the occupied Palestinian territories, including East Jerusalem, and particularly in the Gaza Strip. This draft resolution underscores the high urgency, absolute necessity for the General Assembly to act now, once again, to demand a ceasefire. We should not let the international community to fail again to act swiftly and responsibly.

Over the past 14 months,

Gaza continues to be under relentless siege and military assault by Israel, without conditions, described as appalling and apocalyptic. We must prevent further catastrophic loss of life and destruction. Mr. President, one year ago, in this Assembly, following the veto of a permanent member of the Security Council, 153 countries supported GA resolution ES10/22 demanding a pause, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, compliance by all parties

to their international legal obligation, especially protection of civilians, as well as the release of all hostages.

Unfortunately, that resolution was not followed through.

We must thus ask ourselves how many lives could have been saved, how much suffering avoided,

and how much destruction prevented

if the demands for a ceasefire had been respected, if Israel respected international law, its charter obligation, and listened to the clear voice of conscience of the international

community instead of persisting with its crime, if accountability had been enforced and veto not used to shield these actions.

It is time to change the trajectory to save two million children, women, and men in Gaza, alleviate the suffering,

and provide them with immediate assistance, relief, and hope. Accountability and justice must be pursued, and a path towards peace must be chartered. This must begin with a ceasefire to stop violence and protect innocent civilians from further harm, including by immediate actions in accordance with ICJ provisional measures. Mr. President, today as the casualty has tragically surpassed 150,000 Palestinians, 70 percent of whom are children and women, and with over 1.9 million Gazans displaced

under inhumane conditions, deprived of essentials of life,

we return to this General Assembly with an urgent appeal for collective action.

We cannot remain silent in the face of this situation.

We must uphold our legal, political, humanitarian, and moral obligation. I repeat, our moral obligation. In the face of yet another veto and the Security Council's inability to implement its own resolutions, including resolutions 2735, the General Assembly must act to fulfill its charter duties. Let us urgently and collectively act to establish an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, to silence the gun, to stop the bloodshed, and protect the Palestinian civilian population under Israel's illegal occupation from further harm and to alleviate their dramatic suffering. Mr. President, There is no other way to end this carnage, to save human life. We need an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire.

We need accountability for all grave breaches of international law, including humanitarian and human rights law, perpetrated by Israel, for

all the war crimes, crimes against humanity, and acts of genocides committed. We must end the suffering.

We must begin the path to recovery and swiftly pursue.

Political solution to achieve long overdue justice and freedom for the Palestinian people.

Indonesia thank the 47 co-sponsors of this resolution.

On behalf of the co-sponsors and in the name of justice and humanity, Indonesia urges all member states to support draft resolution L33. Let us act collectively to honour our shared responsibility, uphold international law in this critical moment. I thank you, Mr. President.

Request a written assessment from the Secretary General on the implementation of this resolution within three weeks of its adoption and further request the Secretary General to submit a comprehensive written report within 60 days of the adoption of this resolution, which should include a a needs assessment for Gaza in the short, medium and long term, an elaboration of the humanitarian, social and economic consequences of the conflict in Gaza, and an overview of the work of different parts of the United Nations system relevant to Gaza, along with recommendations on how to strengthen coordination across these parts. Thank you, Mr. President. The resolutions before the Assembly today are beyond logic. They defy all concepts of morality and the evidence we have laid before you for years. By voting for these resolutions, you are not voting to protect humanitarian values, but to protect an organization that has become a haven for terror. You vote for the resolutions knowing the truth. knowing that UNRWA is not a neutral actor but an entity hopelessly infiltrated by Hamas knowing that its facilities have been used to store weapons its schools to indoctrinate children with hatred and its staff to aid and act as terrorists the vote today is not a vote for compassion it is a vote for complicity. As if this betrayal is not enough, you pushed for a resolution that failed to even condition a ceasefire on the release of the 100 hostages still held by Hamas. By demanding a ceasefire today without addressing the hostages, this assembly will once again side with those who weaponize human suffering it will send a message that the lives of innocent Israelis including children are not worth your consideration this is not diplomacy it is appeasement it is enabling Terror and abandoning the innocent today I sit here with evidence in hand letters upon letters that Israel has written to UNRWA over the years each one a warning each one a clear call to action and yet nothing was done Commissioner General Lazzerini complains of reputational damage of so-called disinformation campaign against UNRWA by Israel. I would like to ask Mr. Lazzarini, where were your complaints when Hamas built tunnels under your schools? Where was your outrage when murderers you employed used those schools as terror bases? Where was your accountability when we sent you these letters exposing terrorists on your payroll. In my hand is a letter written in November 2003, 21 years ago, in which we warned about terrorists hiding, meeting, and even training in UNRWA facilities. UNRWA did not act. In 2011, 13 years ago, we warned UNRWA about Hamas operatives working in UNRWA schools. We even provided the names and IDs of 10 Hamas terrorists employed by UNRWA. Nothing was done. In fact, the last name on this list, Najeeh Salam Abu Aziz, was an UNRWA principal, believe it or not. Of course, no action was taken against him. In the meantime, this year, he allowed his school to be used as a launch pad for anti-tank missiles by his fellow Hamas terrorists. In 2017, a Hamas tunnel was discovered beneath an UNRWA school led by a principal who publicly pledged allegiance to Hamas. you again remained silent. Just this July, we provided the names of over 100 UNRWA employees who were members of Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Again, nothing was done. These are only a few examples out of many over the decades. UNRWA's inaction speaks volumes. They did not act when we presented evidence. They did not act when Hamas turned schools into ammunition stores. They did not act when the lives of innocent Israelis were at stake. Now, the New York Times has recently confirmed what we have long known, and I urge you all to read this article in the New York Times. Hamas has infiltrated UNRWA at every level. It is simply a documented fact. To Hamas, UNRWA schools are, and I quote from Hamas's own documents, they call it the best obstacles to shield their terror operations. Gazan residents themselves have admitted to the New York Times that it is a quote, open secret that Hamas operatives work in UNRWA schools, some even carrying Kalashnikovs after class instead of textbooks. Yet this assembly rewards such complicity with continued funding and unwavering support. And now it seeks to demand a ceasefire without conditioning the release of the hostages still suffering in Hamas's dungeons. You will have abandoned them. You will have ignored their families. You will have emboldened their captures. To stand by UNRWA today is to stand by Hamas. The same Hamas that orchestrated the October 7 massacre, that butchered over 1,200 innocent people and that still holds 100 hostages. To demand a ceasefire while ignoring these hostages is to surrender to terror. Distinguished colleagues, a future for Gaza must be one without Hamas, but it must also be one without UNRWA. Without its complicity, aid could flow freely, schools could teach peace instead of hatred, and the people of Gaza could finally begin to rebuild. This Assembly has a choice today, to confront terror and its enablers or to appease them. If you choose to stand by UNRWA and abandon the hostages, you will have chosen appeasement. History will not forget this choice, and neither will we. Thank you, Mr. President.

Thank you very much, Mr. President. the delegation of paraguay is grateful for the opportunity to be able to take the floor to explain our vote before the vote on draft resolution aes ten l thirty two and l thirty three. Otherwise, we will only be postponing a sustainable solution with everyone suffering. The fact that the proponents continue to include different measures to those that will bring about a ceasefire the final goal of resolution l three hundred and thirty three and also insisting on condemning only one of the parties in the text means that this has not reached greater support. We really want a peaceful solution to the situation that will support Israelis and Palestinians and find a balance in the situation. But the text, we feel, do not provide that balance. We cannot support them. Thank you.

Thank you, Mr. President. Regarding statement and explanation of UNGA draft resolution 33, L33, titled Demand for Ceasefire in Gaza.

The Republic of the Marshall Islands.

Welcomes the recent ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon and mediating countries and urges all parties to abide by its terms. Yet other areas of instability, violence, and repression and humanitarian crisis persist in Gaza and nearby. The fate of hostages remain unresolved.

The underlining initial violence and brutal horror of Hamas's October 7 massacre must be condemned and acknowledged, and the perpetrators and collaborators brought to justice.

However, this cannot be the retributive justification.

For the further loss of tens of thousands of civilian lives and a humanitarian crisis. Ending civilian suffering and further loss of life in Gaza broadly requires an urgent ceasefire, unconditional release of hostages, addressing and accounting for the remains of dead hostages, and humanitarian assistance at scale, all elements put together before the UN Security Council. Would be missed.

President, New Zealand welcomes the adoption of today's resolutions and voted in support of the resolutions after careful consideration. The situation in Gaza remains untenable.
