Thank you, Mr. President. At the outset, let me extend our appreciation to Palestine for its initiative and flexibility during the negotiation of the two draft resolutions. I must say that neither of them is perfect. Important elements are missing, such as clear and strong condemnation of Hamas' brutal acts of terror and their continued hostage-taking in violation of international law. However, both of the resolutions represent a much-needed display of political will of the international community. The tragedy in Gaza is never-ending. Every passing day brings additional casualties of innocent civilians and increases the suffering of both Palestinians and Israelis, including the hostages. The humanitarian situation, which is already described as apocalyptic, is getting worse as time goes by. Although it is too late to save those lives already lost, The need for immediate ceasefire, the release of all remaining hostages, and the drastic expansion of humanitarian aid to Gaza remains crucial. These are the pillars of the ceasefire resolution and what Japan has consistently advocated for the Security Council. It is also essential now to preserve UNRWA. The agency is the backbone of humanitarian assistance to the more than two million desperate people of Gaza. The agency will also play a critical role to rebuild humanitarian human dignity of Palestinian refugees after a post ceasefire period. However, this indispensable organization is at the brink of collapse following the adoption of the two Knesset laws severely restricting the operation. Our concerted efforts to maintain the agency are urgently needed. This is the aim of this resolution and Japan fully shares this objective. At the same time, this resolution contains an important call for UNRWA to fully implement the recommendations of the Independent Review Group and Japan supports this aspect as well. Therefore, we voted in favour of the two draft resolutions. Having said that, today's Today's adoption is not the end goal, as nothing will change if the resolutions remain solely on paper. We have a collective responsibility to make sure that this Assembly's demands are addressed by the parties. For this purpose, we must not overlook the importance of a negotiated settlement between the parties. In this vein, Japan is encouraged by the reports on the resumption of ceasefire talks and the tireless efforts of the mediators. Finally, Japan is steadfastly committed to a lasting peace for both Israel and Palestine in the form of two-state solution, and will continue to make all possible diplomatic efforts to this end. Likewise, we will remain at the forefront of humanitarian assistance, to the most vulnerable and also stand ready to contribute to the early recovery and reconstruction of Gaza. I thank you.
I thank Japan. I give the floor to Guatemala.

President, since 1947 Guatemala has maintained its firm conviction that peaceful coexistence between the Israeli people and the Palestinian people must be based on the preeminence of international law. As a state that has a solid pacifist vocation, we recognize the need to find a peaceful solution to the conflict, advocating that this be facilitated by the international community and that the United Nations sponsor a political process aimed at promoting a just and sustainable peace in the region, with the involvement of all parties concerned. This is only possible with a two-state solution which addresses the legitimate security concerns of Israel and allows for the building of a Palestinian state which would be politically and economically viable. We believe that the state of Palestine should coexist alongside Israel according to clearly defined borders that are secure, peaceful and internationally recognized in accordance with the relevant resolutions of the United Nations. However, whilst working on this desire for peace, Guatemala recognises the vital and singular work done by the United Nations Relief and Works Agency in the Near East, which, under the mandate granted by this General Assembly, aims to guarantee access to education, health care, humanitarian assistance and social services to the refugees of Palestine. an organisation which, as was pointed out by its head recently, is the only pillar of life left standing for Palestinians, because without its work the humanitarian response of the United Nations would collapse. Mr. President, as we have said on various occasions, the veto of any draft resolution that calls for a ceasefire shows the paralysis of the Security Council, the highest organ charged with maintaining international peace and security. Once again, we advocate avoiding the exercise of the veto when dealing with preventing or stopping situations involving mass atrocities. Also, Guatemala highlights the need for the Security Council to adopt resolutions that take into account, in a balanced way, all elements that would allow for an immediate ceasefire and an end to hostilities and atrocities between the parties involved. the urgency of ensuring humanitarian assistance in Gaza and also the release of all hostages with the aim of protecting the human rights of the people affected. Guatemala reiterates that it is ready to support all efforts aimed at establishing a lasting peace in the region, anchored in mutual respect and full adherence to international law. It is for these reasons that Guatemala today has supported the two draft resolutions that were presented. Thank you very much.
I thank Guatemala. I give the floor to Australia.

Thank you, President. I will speak to both the resolutions we have considered today. Although Australia does not agree with everything in the resolution entitled Support for the Mandate of UNRWA, Our vote in favour reflects our view that UNRWA must be able to continue its lifesaving work. That is also why Australia has funded the organisation every year since 1951. UNRWA provides desperately needed services to civilians in the occupied Palestinian territories and across the region. As the Security Council has said, UNRWA is the backbone of the humanitarian response to the catastrophic situation in Gaza. We join the Security Council in expressing grave concern over legislation adopted by the Israeli Knesset. Limiting UNRWA's operations will only exacerbate an already terrible humanitarian crisis. As stated in this resolution, UNRWA has a responsibility to address any credible allegations and to ensure accountability for any violations of the agency's principles of neutrality, impartiality and independence. We acknowledge the commitment made by the United Nations Secretary-General and UNRWA to implement fully the recommendations of the independent review led by Catherine Colonna. We call for their accelerated implementation in line with UNRWA's commitment to the principle of neutrality. We note UNRWA's measures to terminate the employment of UNRWA staff members following the 7 October atrocities carried out by Hamas, atrocities that should have been unequivocally condemned by this resolution. Any involvement or affiliation with terrorist organisations cannot be tolerated. Australia will continue to press the United Nations and UNRWA to safeguard the organisation's neutrality. Australia reiterates calls for the protection of humanitarian and United Nations personnel, including UNRWA staff, to enable them to perform their lifesaving work. The best protection for humanitarian personnel and civilians is ceasefire. Australia will continue to support a strong and robust multilateral system, including the protection of United Nations agencies to do their critical work. In relation to the resolution entitled Demand for Ceasefire in Gaza, I wish to address certain reservations, but first I will outline why Australia voted in favour. First, Australia is committed to working with the international community to end this conflict, to stop the suffering, and immediately and unconditionally to secure the release of all hostages held by Hamas. Tomorrow marks one year since Australia joined 152 other countries in voting for a ceasefire in this assembly. Further delay will only see more lives lost. Second, This resolution's demand for full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian assistance to Gaza has never been more necessary. The current situation in Gaza is catastrophic. The human suffering unbearable. In Israel's response to Hamas atrocities on October 7, more than 44,000 Palestinians have been killed, including more than 13,000 children. Nearly all of Gaza's 2.1 million people have lost their homes, and do not have enough food, water, medicine or shelter. Third, along with the international community, Australia reiterates our call on all parties to comply fully with international law. Civilians and humanitarian workers must be protected. Israel must take urgent action to alleviate this humanitarian crisis in line with the binding orders of the International Court of Justice. Fourth, Australia supports this resolution's unwavering commitment to the vision of a two-state solution because it is the only way out of this terrible cycle of violence. Fifth, we support this resolution because of its call for the immediate and unconditional release of hostages and the urgency of the current crisis. In terms of reservations, we support the United States proposal for an immediate ceasefire deal with the release of hostages as endorsed by the United Nations Security Council. Ceasefires have conditions that parties must agree. This reality should have been reflected in the resolution. The fact it has not is a shortcoming. Moreover, Australia remains unequivocal in our condemnation of Hamas. This resolution should have done the same for their atrocities on 7 October that left 1,200 Israelis dead and more than 200 hostages taken, and all their acts of terror. Australia repeats our demand for Hamas to release all hostages immediately and unconditionally. Hamas must lay down their arms. There can be no role for terrorists in the future governance of Gaza. Finally, President, Australia continues to give careful consideration to the International Court of Justice's conclusions in its advisory opinion. Our vote is not determinative of Australia's position on all the conclusions in that opinion, including those recalled in this resolution. Thank you, President.
I thank Australia. I give the floor to Chechia.

Thank you, Mr. President. As we gather here today, the Middle East is engulfed in profound turmoil. My country, Czechia, is deeply troubled by the ongoing suffering endured by civilians in the region. We are deeply concerned about the critical situation of the civilian population in Gaza, who deserve to live in peace and dignity. We welcome any meaningful efforts to end the violence. Let me acknowledge that both resolutions adopted today contain a number of constructive elements that represent positive progress. We commend the efforts to find common ground and address the urgent challenges in the region. However, we must not overlook the horrific terrorist attacks of the 7th of October that plunged the region into this current cycle of conflict. Hamas terrorists unleashed a deadly rampage, brutally killing and maiming innocent civilians and taking hostages in a shocking display of barbarity. There can be no excuse or justification for such egregious acts, which have had fatal consequences for all people in the region. Once again, my government regrets that this esteemed assembly did not take a more forceful stance in condemning the actions of Hamas. Moreover, the resolution L33 fails to unequivocally link a durable ceasefire to the release of all the hostages. To omit this crucial linkage risks sending a dangerously misguided signal to Hamas that their reckless reign of terror may somehow be vindicated. We must not abandon the hostages and their families. It is due to this omission that the Czech Republic cannot support this resolution, and that is why we voted against it. Let us be clear Hamas too has a choice to make. They could immediately release the hostages They could cease using civilians as human shields and stop exploiting civilian infrastructure to launch terrorist attacks. It is Hamas terrorists who have imperiled millions of Palestinian civilians. Mr. President, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza has reached a critical juncture. The population is in dire need of food, water, medical supplies, and other essential items. While we fully support urgent calls to step up the delivery of vital humanitarian aid, we must also acknowledge and rectify certain operational shortcomings within UNRWA. We must make every effort to ensure beyond any shadow of a doubt that Hamas and other terrorist groups cannot exploit the existing system for distributing critical assistance. Equally important is guaranteeing strict neutrality, accountability and oversight in all aspects of UNRWA's operations. In this respect, we continue to closely monitor and evaluate the implementation of the recommendations of the Independent Review Group. The resolution L32 in our assessment does not sufficiently address these pressing concerns. Therefore, we have decided to abstain from voting on this resolution. Distinguished colleagues, I would like to conclude by emphasising that re establishing a political horizon for a two state solution remains of paramount importance. A negotiated settlement remains the single path to guaranteeing security, political stability and democratic development for both Israel and Palestine. We encourage regional actors to pursue a course of cooperation, including through the Abraham Accords, to build a brighter future for the Middle East. Rather than introducing new initiatives here in New York, we need positive developments on the ground in the region itself. I thank you.
I thank Chekya. I give the floor to Hungary.

Mr. President, we are here today to discuss the dire humanitarian situation and the demand for an end to the conflict in Gaza. We must not forget that the conflict that the General Assembly seeks to end by imposing an unconditional ceasefire was ignited by the horrendous and brutal acts of terrorism committed by Hamas on October 7, 2023. Any country would have the right and responsibility to ensure that such an attack could never happen again, as permitted under IHO it has been more than a year since the terrorist attacks that led to the escalation of the conflict which has caused the devastating humanitarian crisis on October 7th 2023 1,195 people were murdered in Israel a further 5,432 people have been injured and 251 have been taken hostage since then More than 43,000 people have been killed in Gaza, and many more have been injured. Hostages are still being held, and innumerable survivors are traumatized. The picture today is catastrophic, and we express our solidarity with Israeli and Palestinian innocent civilians caught in the conflict. There are no excuses left for Hamas to continue rejecting the ceasefire and put innocent Palestinian civilians at risk every day. It is high time for this conflict to end, for the hostages to be released, and for Palestinian civilians to begin rebuilding their lives. However, the fighting must end in a sustainable way. A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas is the only way to bring about a durable end to this conflict. But Hamas has failed to accept any agreement so far that would bring hostages home, ensure Israel's security, enable a surge in humanitarian relief to Palestinians, and set the stage for a political settlement which can provide a better future for Israelis and Palestinians alike. All civilian life matters equally. We note with utmost concern the unacceptable number of civilian casualties, especially children, as well as the catastrophic levels of hunger and imminent risk of famine caused by the insufficient entry of aid into Gaza.

It is time for this conflict to end.

The only durable way to resolve this conflict is to establish a ceasefire that also guarantees the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held in Gaza. These two urgent goals are inextricably linked. An unconditional ceasefire would mean that hostages would likely never return home. We once again call on Hamas and other terrorist groups within Gaza to release all remaining hostages immediately without precondition, cease hostilities, and spare all civilians from further suffering. We recall that there is still a Hungarian citizen being held hostage by the terrorists. Right now, the international community must focus on implementing the existing framework for resolving the conflict. Security Council Resolution 2735, which offers a glimmer of hope for the peaceful settlement of this conflict and gives diplomacy a chance. Hungary calls for the full implementation of Security Council Resolution 2735 without delay and without conditions, which would lead to an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, a significant and sustained increase in flow of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza.
I thank Hungary. I give the floor to Germany.

Mr. President, Germany voted in favor of the two resolutions. We call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and the unconditional release of all hostages. The unbearable suffering that followed the heinous terrorist attacks on 7th of October of last year must cease immediately for the sake of Palestinians in Gaza and the hostages and their families. A lasting peace in the region can only be achieved through a negotiated two-state solution. Only when Israel's security is ensured and Palestinians have their own state where they can live in dignity and safety will both peoples be able to live side by side in peace. Germany, alongside its partners, remains steadfast in its commitment to work towards this goal. Mr. President, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. We urgently need a humanitarian surge as winter starts. Israel must uphold its commitment to flood Gaza with aid and that access be guaranteed at all times. Germany is the second largest contributor of humanitarian aid to Gaza and together with our partners has consistently been and continues to be engaged in substantive financial and diplomatic humanitarian support to increase the flow of aid into Gaza in order to alleviate the unimaginable suffering of the Palestinians there. At this critical moment, UNRWA's role is essential. Germany remains steadfast in its commitment to supporting UNRWA and Palestinians in need in Gaza and across the region. UNRWA remains indispensable for delivering essential support to millions of Palestinian refugees in Gaza, East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and across the entire regions. Against this backdrop, Germany is gravely concerned about the adoption of two laws targeting UNRWA by the Knesset. UNRWA must, as well as other UN organizations and agencies, must be fully able to deliver humanitarian aid and assistance to save lives and ease the suffering. We urge the Israeli government to abide by its international obligations, respect the privileges and immunities of UNRWA, and live up to its responsibility to facilitate full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian assistance to the civilian population in Gaza. We commend UNRWA for taking steps to address allegations regarding individual employees support for terrorist organizations and to pursue and implement reforms of internal processes. We expect UNRWA to continue its path of reform, demonstrating its commitment to the principle of neutrality, treat allegations swiftly and as a matter of priority, and ensure that its activities remain entirely in line with its mandate. We will continue to actively monitor and support this process. Germany unequivocally condemns the horrific attacks carried out by Hamas and other terrorist groups on October 7, 2023, as well as the consistent attacks against Israel by these terrorist groups, and we call on the General Assembly to do the same. Germany remains committed to the security of Israel. Israel, like all states, has the right to defend itself against armed attacks by terrorists and extremists. At the same time, this right must be exercised in line with international humanitarian law, and accountability of all sides needs to be ensured. On accountability, we are in favor of strengthening the existing structures rather than creating new ones, which could result in duplication. Additional mechanisms could weaken rather than strengthen the pursuit of justice and peace. Mr. President, the entire region is undergoing historic changes. The ceasefire agreement in Lebanon offers hope. The abhorrent dictatorship in Syria has fallen. Let us work together now with determination and commitment to stop the suffering in Gaza, to liberate the hostages, and to lay the foundation for a more peaceful Middle East, a Middle East where Israelis, Palestinians, and all people in the region can live side by side in peace and security. Germany remains fully committed to this goal. I thank you.
I thank Germany. I give the floor to Bulgaria.

Thank you, Mr. President. I take the floor to deliver an explanation of vote on resolution L 32, support for the mandate of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East. For Gary is gravely alarmed by the catastrophic situation of civilians in Gaza and reiterates its call for an uninterrupted, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and aid to reach those in need through all necessary measures. While recognizing UNRWA's important and indispensable role in providing humanitarian relief and essential services to Palestine refugees and acknowledging the steps taken towards greater accountability, we are of the view that the resolution does not sufficiently address the need for robust safeguards to reinforce neutrality, operational transparency, and impartiality in UNRWA's activities. For that reason, Bulgaria was not in a position to support it. Bulgaria underscores the importance of upholding the humanitarian principles, ensuring the neutrality and accountability of aid organisations and pursuing durable solutions that address both immediate needs and long term challenges. Thank you.
I thank Bulgaria. I give the floor to Belgium.

Mr. President, Belgium voted in favour of the two draft resolutions and we fully support the main elements contained therein an immediate ceasefire respected by all parties, the immediate unconditional release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access to civilians and, until there is a sustainable solution to the conflict, the essential implementation of UNRWA's mandate. Dear colleagues, we need to break with this dialogue of the deaf that we have been seeing and work towards a common solution. Break with the cycle of violence, break with the dehumanisation and hate speech. Diplomacy must return, as it was able to in Lebanon. This requires concessions on both sides. Nothing can justify the massacre of more than 40,000 civilians in Gaza and elsewhere. Only an immediate ceasefire can put a stop to the unacceptable suffering that is being inflicted on the people. Belgium urges parties to demonstrate goodwill so that these negotiations can finally lead somewhere. This horror must end. and nothing can justify the taking of civilian hostages. The hostages that have been detained since the 7th of October must be immediately and unconditionally released. Families must know the fate of their missing loved ones. This is also the case for those detained, particularly minors. The There should be a path that leads towards a two-state solution, two states, democratic states, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace within safe and recognized borders. This has been approved by the Security Council. It is now time to act, to prevent and condemn terrorism. Let's condemn in the strongest terms the barbaric terrorist acts perpetrated by Hamas on the 7th of October. The necessary conditions need to be created to promote peace and negotiations. Let us join the collective work of the Global Alliance to give life to a two-state solution. Finally, the negative trends need to be reversed. Let us work to implement the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice on the illegal nature of these settlements, and let us categorically reject the continuing expansionist policy carried out by Israel. We are very concerned by the rumours of annexation of Palestinian territories and the transfer of the administration of occupied territories towards civilian administration. Only a political path leads to peace and reconciliation. We expect a greater and stronger commitment to this end on the part of those involved. In absence of a political solution, UNRWA's indispensable work must continue. The disinformation campaign against it is unacceptable. Equally, the application, enforcement of laws adopted by the Knesset in violation of Israel's obligation under international law is a disastrous precedent for the multilateral system. Belgium welcomes the letter of the Secretary-General from the 9th of December on this topic and aligns itself with its content. Belgium never suspended its funding for the agency and has committed to it in the long term via a multi-year, three-year agreement. We invite the members, particularly those who have the means but have not yet contributed to the financing of UNRWA, to do the same and to honour their commitments. The effective implementation of the Colonna report is important too in order to improve UNRWA's neutrality. We commend the efforts already undertaken by the agency in this end. Further efforts are crucial with our collective support. Finally, Belgium supports the initiatives that guarantee accountability. International law and international humanitarian law cannot be applied selectively. because otherwise they would be weakened as a whole. Thank you very much.
I thank Belgium. I give the floor to the Republic of Korea.

Mr. President, last month, as one of the elected members of the Security Council, the Republic of Korea participated

in proposing a draft resolution to the Council demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire

in parallel with demanding an immediate and unconditional release of hostages. The Republic of Korea believes that in order to urgently save lives and alleviate the extreme suffering of Palestinians in Gaza, an immediate ceasefire is not an option, but an imperative. Based on this belief, we co-pled the E10 draft resolution coordinated by Guyana last month. Additionally, We voted in favor of the draft resolution today, reiterating this demand for an immediate ceasefire. However, this does not mean that we forgot about the hostages still brutally held in Gaza. We must remember what happened on October 7th last year and how the current conflict in Gaza was brought about. Thus, we take note that the draft resolution today clearly reiterates the GA's demand for the release of all hostages.

Having said that, the Republic of Korea

would like to point out that the establishment of any new mechanisms for accountability should be scrupulously assessed within the context of the existing ones. This includes, but is not limited to, various committees, commission of inquiry, and courts with the jurisdictions over the occupied Palestine territory. The Republic of Korea also voted in favor of the resolution to support the mandate of UNRWA. We believe that the continued operation of UNRWA is crucial, not only to support the humanitarian efforts in Gaza, but also to provide millions of Palestinian refugees in the OPT and beyond with basic services, including education and healthcare. As such, we call on all key stakeholders, notably Israel, to seriously consider the possible consequences of suspending or obstructing the mandate of UNRWA, which may exacerbate the security in the region.

With regard to the resolution on UNRWA adopted today, the Republic of Korea would like to clarify our view

that this resolution does not include any new budgetary implications or financial commitments beyond the scope of

what has been previously discussed in the Fifth Committee and approved by the GA. The Republic of Korea, as one of the members of the Security Council, will constructively participate in all efforts to restore peace and stability in the Middle East. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the Republic of Korea. I give the floor to Austria.

Thank you, Mr. President. Austria voted in favor of draft resolution L-33 entitled Demand for a Ceasefire in Gaza and abstained on draft resolution L-32 entitled Support for the Mandate of UNRWA. Permit me to explain our reasoning. The barbaric terror attack of Hamas against Israel 14 months ago, which we condemned in the strongest possible terms, brought a new dimension of devastation to the region. Israelis are traumatized by the slaughter, torture, and sexual violence of October 7th of last year. Over 100 hostages are still held captive by Hamas terrorists, including an Austrian father of two. In Gaza, the civilian population is facing starvation and disease in which can only be described a humanitarian catastrophe. The destruction and devastation in Gaza has reached unacceptable levels with too many civilian lives lost already. International humanitarian law is non-negotiable. It applies all the time, everywhere. The protection of civilians is paramount. We therefore simply need an urgent ceasefire in Gaza to achieve the release of all remaining hostages and scale up the delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza. Draft resolution L33 on a ceasefire in Gaza links the demand for a ceasefire respected by all parties to the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and also calls for the full implementation of Security Council Resolution 2735 on a ceasefire and release of hostages, which we fully support. We also recognize and support the efforts by regional partners and the United States in this regard. For these reasons, we voted yes on draft resolution L.33. With a view to resolution L32 on UNRWA, Austria is deeply concerned about recent developments surrounding the agency, including the Israeli legislation adopted by the Knesset on 28 October, effectively halting the vital work of UNRWA in Gaza and the West Bank will not add to Israel's security and stability, but instead have long-lasting and probably devastating consequences for the humanitarian situation in the occupied Palestinian territories. At the same time, the agency must also continue on its path for reforms. We closely studied the report and findings of the independent review group chaired by former Foreign Minister Catherine Kolonna, set up after the allegations that UNRWA staff members were involved in Hamas terror attack on Israel last year. We welcome the commitment of the Secretary-General and the agency's leadership to fully implement these recommendations. And we welcome that the resolution adopted today clearly calls on UNOWA to fully implement the high-level action plan developed by the agency as a follow-up to the recommendations. We will continue to closely monitor the implementation of the action plan together with our international partners. Many of these elements are reflected in the draft resolution adopted today. However, we would have wished to see an even stronger focus on the need for reform of the organization. For the sake of its own credibility, the UN must simply be beyond reproach. Finally, the text does not address the misuse of UNRWA premises by Hamas and other terrorist groups for military purposes. For these reasons, Austria abstained on this resolution. Two short final points, colleagues. First, Austrian development cooperation continues to strive within the framework of bilateral and multilateral cooperation with partners such as UNRWA to improve the situation of the Palestinians. Since 7 October 2023, Austria has provided 53 million euros in humanitarian aid for the civilian population in Gaza and the conflict ridden region, including 3.4 million for UNRWA. As always, let me underline that Austria reconfirms its commitment to a negotiated two-state solution and to a viable Palestinian state living side by side in peace and security with Israel, with Gaza being an integral part of the future Palestinian state. Thank you.
I thank Austria. I give the floor to Switzerland.

Mr President, Switzerland voted in favour of the two resolutions. This is the expression of our great concern when faced with the suffering of civilians in the Middle East and the importance that Switzerland attaches to respect for international law and Switzerland's strong support for the central role of the UN for peace stability and humanitarian aid in the region. Conflict in the Middle East, particularly the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip, requires our urgent action and also that of the Security Council. As an elected member of the Council, Switzerland has actively contributed to the draft resolution considered by the Council in November and voted in favour of it. We believe that no member of the Council should have voted against a draft like the one that was presented collectively by the ten elected members. Unfortunately, this is not the first veto since the acts of terror on the 7th of October that we strongly condemned. Switzerland has a long-standing commitment to a restricted use of the veto at the Security Council. We would also recall the code of conduct the Act Code of Conduct, which has supported more than two thirds of the members of this assembly so far. Despite this veto, we have a responsibility to continue to give our full attention to resolving this devastating conflict. Switzerland recalls that international law, including international humanitarian law and human rights law, is binding on parties irrespective of Parties must respect their obligations in all circumstances. In addition, Switzerland shares the strong concern expressed by the General Assembly today regarding the law adopted by the Knesset against UNRWA on 28 October. These are largely incompatible with international law. UNRWA is the largest humanitarian actor in Gaza and provides vital services to more than two million people. Switzerland expects that Israel respect its obligations under international law, including the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. We would also recall that, as the occupying power, Israel has the duty to ensure that the essential needs of the people in the occupied Palestinian territory are met. UNRWA is subject to a large scepticism. in Switzerland following the reproaches of some of its workers allegedly participating in the Hamas attacks on the 7th of October. Hence, our support to the resolution on UNRWA reflects our call on UNRWA to continue its reform works and fully implement the recommendations from the Colonna report. Any allegation of violation of UNRWA's neutrality should be followed up on. and adequate measures should be taken. The effectiveness with which the challenges will be addressed will be determining, crucial for the future of the organisation. Regarding the appeal in the resolution to increase voluntary contributions to UNRWA, Switzerland would underscore that any decision on Swiss support is subject to the approval of our Parliament. President, in the face of so much suffering, words are beginning to fail us. What can we say except that we must act and defend together the values and founding principles of our international order? Humanity must prevail. What can we say other than that we know the solution? We repeat it, an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of hostages, and the respect for international law, including the protection of civilians, and the safe, rapid and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid starting immediately. We urgently need to revive the prospects for peace based on a two state solution so that Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace, security and dignity. It is high time to do exactly that. Thank you.
I thank Switzerland. I give the floor to Romania.

Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, Romania voted in favor of the two resolutions adopted earlier today, as my delegation is a strong believer in using all diplomatic resorts, including UN avenues, to achieve the long-standing political objective, two-state solution. This remains the only way for bringing just and lasting peace in the Middle East with the state of Israel and an independent, democratic, contiguous, sovereign and viable state of Palestine living side by side in peace and security and mutual recognition. However, Romania would have preferred a strong condemnation in the text of the horrific Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023, which resulted not only in hundreds of dead Israeli civilians, but also hostages for whose lives we fear. We cannot but repeat the need for the hostages to be released immediately and unconditionally. The humanitarian situation in Gaza has reached a low point that could not be imagined 15 months ago. We pay tribute to all UN agencies and member states, including my own, that contribute for the benefit of the civilians in Gaza. UNRWA remains a key instrument in responding to the needs of the Palestine refugees in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, West Bank and Gaza. We welcome the measures taken to implement the recommendations of the Colonna report on UNRWA activities. This is the kind of scrutiny that needs to monitor the intended mandate given by this General Assembly to UNRWA in December 1949. I thank you, Mr President.
I thank Romania. I give the floor to Sweden.

Britain remains committed to a just and comprehensive resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict with the state of Israel and an independent, democratic, contiguous, sovereign and viable state of Palestine living side by side in peace and security and mutual recognition, with Jerusalem as a future capital of both states in accordance with the relevant resolutions of the UN Security Council. Sweden shares the deep concern expressed over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the immense suffering of the civilian population. We reiterate our condemnation of the abhorrent terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October last year. All remaining hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally. International law, including international humanitarian law, must be respected by all parties.

There is an urgent need for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza in line with Security Council Resolution 2735. Sweden fully supports the diplomatic efforts to this end.

We are deeply concerned by the recent legislation on UNRWA adopted by Israel and urge Israeli authorities

to ensure continued humanitarian access to the many civilians who depend on UN services. We expect that UNRWA, like other UN agencies, is respected and protected in line with international obligations.

We reiterate that the legislation, if implemented, may violate Israel's obligations under international

law, including international humanitarian law, and the legally binding provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice.

We welcome the call on all parties to ensure respect for the principles of humanity, neutrality,

impartiality, and independence for the provision of humanitarian assistance.

Mr President, Sweden voted in favour of the resolution on ceasefire in Gaza, as well as the

resolution on support for the mandate of UNRWA today.

Nonetheless, Sweden would like to clarify its position related to the UNRWA resolution, notably operative paragraph seven and 31. The text of the resolution is in certain aspects more far-reaching than what has previously been agreed by this Assembly.

Sweden would have preferred a more balanced approach, highlighting the crucial role

of UNRWA, as well as the need for necessary measures to safeguard the UN's ability to find sustainable solutions to ensure the continued delivery of humanitarian aid to Palestine refugees. Finally, we would like to thank the UN humanitarian staff for their tireless work on the ground, often at the risk of their lives.

We deeply regret the deaths of UN humanitarian workers and express our heartfelt condolences to their families.

Thank you.
I thank Sweden. I give the floor to the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Thank you, Mr. President. And I thank you for convening today's emergency special session. I have the honor to deliver this explanation of vote on the resolution on the demand for ceasefire in Gaza and the resolution on UNRWA on behalf of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Mr. President, it has been more than a year since the atrocious attacks by Hamas on 7 October 2023. And to our grave concern, the prospects remain bleak. The conflict that unfolded after the attacks is still ongoing. The fate of many of the hostages is still uncertain, and the suffering of the people in Gaza is worsening every day. A year has passed, and still more than 100 people are held hostage, and for more than 400 days, their families have been living in the greatest fear for their loved ones. In this light, the Kingdom of the Netherlands reiterates and that the end of this horrific war must be linked to the release of these hostages. We call for an immediate ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the unimpeded delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid to those in need. Concerns about UNRWA should be addressed and recommendations on the neutrality of UNRWA from the Colonna report need to be implemented. Nonetheless, restricting the work of UNRWA in a time of unprecedented humanitarian needs, will negatively impact the already worrying situation in the region and especially in Gaza. We urge Israel to carefully consider its international obligations and the impact on the ground before taking further action. The ban on UNRWA poses a concern for the ability to deliver humanitarian aid to people in need in Gaza. Therefore, the Netherlands supports most of what is stated in the resolution tabled here today on UNRWA. Nevertheless, at this moment, the continuity of humanitarian aid delivery is too reliant on the implementing capacity of one organisation. While supporting the mandate of UNRWA in providing basic services in the region and thereby contributing to stability, we therefore abstained from voting. The Netherlands will continue to provide humanitarian assistance through various channels, and we support efforts to further diversify the humanitarian landscape in Gaza to better guarantee that humanitarian aid can reach those in need. Today, we also reaffirm our longstanding commitment to pursuing accountability for international crimes and other violations of international law committed by any of the parties of the conflict. We strongly believe that pushing for justice promotes a shared sense of hope, commitment, and duty. The Kingdom of the Netherlands welcomes the request to the Secretary-General to present proposals on how the United Nations could help advance accountability and underlines the importance that existing and possible new mechanisms should reinforce and complement each other. The Kingdom of the Netherlands has therefore voted in favour of the resolution on the ceasefire in Gaza in front of us today and abstained on the UNRWA resolution. I thank you very much.
I thank the Kingdom of the Netherlands. I give the floor to Liechtenstein.

Mr. President, Liechtenstein has voted in favour of resolution ES 10/25 just adopted entitled Support for the Mandate of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East. We know that much of this text is similar to that of resolution 78/73 adopted last year with overwhelming support of the membership, including our own. We note furthermore that additions to the text reflect the vastly deteriorated situation in Gaza and the need to ensure the full implementation of the recommendations of the Colonna report, including through the necessary funding, which is essential for the effective continued operation of UNRWA with full respect for the principle of neutrality. Liechtenstein reiterates, as the Security Council has, and as this resolution does that UNRWA remains the backbone of all humanitarian response in Gaza and that no organization can replace or substitute UNRWA's capacity and mandate to serve Palestine refugees and civilians in urgent need of life-saving humanitarian assistance. Our vote in favor of this resolution is a vote to support UNRWA's efforts to meet the needs of Palestinian civilians and to meet the high standards of governance that we expect from it. To this end, we also continue to support the statement of shared commitments on UNRWA proposed by Kuwait, Jordan, and Slovenia. I thank you.
I thank Liechtenstein. I give the floor to Iraq.

Mr. President, Iraq has voted in favor of Resolution A/ES10/L.33 as an expression of its firm position in support of the just Palestinian cause and the support of all international efforts that aim to put an end to the aggression and the systematic violations of the occupying powers. Thank you, sir.

And also the resolution defending UNRWA and on the basis of its mandate stemming from the General Assembly. What we need is an immediate ceasefire, unconditional, And what we need is UNRWA to be able to carry out the humanitarian assistance needed to our people in Gaza, including the northern part of Gaza. As I said, we are grateful and thankful to this overwhelming support. It's almost unanimous vote on these two resolutions. This reflect the resolve and the determination of the international community as we see it reflected in this very important chamber, the General Assembly, which is the highest authority in the UN system.
